behavior: AC1 — one run, one transaction, one ledger row: a failing run leaves zero data rows, zero success rows and exactly one error row written after the rollback; a successful run commits its success row with its data

AC2 — atomicity is not broken by the repositories: with BEGIN IMMEDIATE open a repository write cannot end the caller's transaction, a mid-batch failure rolls back every row of that batch, and a bare commit() inside the explicit transaction is pinned as the negative control

AC3 — the window rule is per class and bounded: minute-truncated UTC for activities, the local GARSYNC_TZ day (today) for the daily classes, a 14-day floor, a 30-day gap closed in <=14-day chunks, and the measured call arithmetic

AC4 — the cursor is a coverage watermark: a zero-row run still advances it, a failed run does not, it is never the run's wall clock, it is read by ledger id rather than created_at, and the activities cursor stays NULL until SUB-003
AC5 — no lock is held across the fetch: a blocking client stub observes conn.in_transaction is False and a second writer commits while it is blocked

AC6 — idempotency is literal and proven on a strictly narrower payload: byte-identical re-pull changes nothing, a narrower payload loses no known value in activities, daily_metrics or sleep_sessions, and a real value change still lands

AC7 — the ledger counts reality: rows_upserted is the number of rows whose values changed, rows_fetched is what the adapter returned, and the declared canonical-serialisation pass is the only one allowed to report changes
AC8 — nothing reads updated_at as a change signal: every occurrence in src/ is a write, and no incremental decision is taken from a row timestamp
AC9 — SC-02(3) is answerable from committed data alone (asked-nothing-yet and no-data-for-day-D) and no raw_payload table exists before its first real writer
AC10 — /api/sync/status and the four route suites are unchanged and green, and the whole gate passes without lowering the coverage baseline
AC11 — the knowledge is recorded in this PR: the ADR-008 amendment exists and every new lesson is paired with its docs/lessons/_index.md row

AC12 — the migration is additive and idempotent: 0003 lands the same schema from a v1 fixture and from a v2 database, adds only rows_fetched/started_at, and the real database is still only migrated on a tmp_path copy
verification: poetry run pytest tests/test_migrations.py -q -k 'Revision0003 or upgrading_twice'
